title: Every factor below the bound divides a bounded product
statement: For a function f on the naturals and indices i < k: f applied to i divides the product of f over the range [0, k).

formal.statement: theorem Nat.dvd_prodRange_of_lt : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat.lt x1 x2) -> AxNat.dvd (x0 x1) (AxNat.prodRange x0 x2)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.dvd_prodRange_of_lt is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- dvd_prodRange_of_lt 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.dvd_prodRange_of_lt[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted kernel gate. The pattern is ANCHORED at the start of the line: `Nat.not_pow_succ_dvd_prodRange_of_lt` contains this theorem's name as a substring, so an unanchored match would pass on the wrong row.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat environment admits no trusted declaration
evidence.notes: Reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0` over the FULL trusted surface (Axiom, Opaque and Quotient), not `Declaration::Axiom` alone, and exits non-zero unless the surface is empty. The enumeration is per-environment rather than per-theorem; it bounds this theorem's footprint because a proof cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain. Read directly from `Kernel::axiom_footprint` for these ten `Nat.Multiset.*` theorems, `theorem_axiom_footprint` prints footprint size 0 and an empty axiom column for every one.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type; declared by `nat_prelude/multiset.rs` (lane nat-multiset, ADR-1520).

notes: Induction on the bound `k`. `Nat.prodRange f (succ j)` reduces to `prodRange f j * f j`, so the step is `dvd_mul_right_of_dvd` on the induction hypothesis when `i < j` and `dvd_mul_left` transported along `f i = f j` when `i = j`. Declared in `nat_prelude/multiset.rs`, its first consumer; it mentions no multiset.
